751: Nothing but money can make people who count for nothing into people who count for something. There is nothing else like it.
752: Everyone looks down on people who have nothing, and everyone praises people who are rich.
753: Money is a lamp that never goes out. Take it to any land you choose, and it drives away the darkness there, most of all the darkness of enemies.
754: Money earned the right way, without doing anything wrong, brings both goodness and happiness.
755: Do not hold on to money that comes without kindness and love. Let it go.
756: A king’s money comes from property that has no owner, from taxes on goods and roads, and from payments made by enemies he has beaten.
757: Kindness is the child born to love, and it is brought up by a rich nanny called money.
758: Starting a job with money already in hand is like watching an elephant fight from a hilltop. You are safe and can see everything.
759: Build up your money. No blade is sharper than money for cutting down the pride of your enemies.
760: For people who have earned plenty of money honestly, the other two goals of life, doing good and being happy, come easily.
761: An army that has every part it needs and wins without fear of getting hurt is the greatest treasure a king can own.
762: Only an army with a long history has the courage to stand firm after losses, unafraid of wounds even when its numbers have shrunk.
763: So what if a crowd of rats roars like the sea? One hiss from a cobra and they all run away and are destroyed.
764: A true army is one that has never been beaten, cannot be bribed by the enemy, and has courage passed down from its fathers.
765: A true army is one that can stand together and fight even if Death himself comes at it in anger.
766: Bravery, honor, following the good example of earlier soldiers, and being trustworthy are the four things that keep an army safe.
767: A true army knows how to stop an attack, and it moves forward by pushing back the front line of the enemy.
768: Even if an army cannot attack well or hold its ground, it can still win fame by looking strong and well equipped.
769: An army will win if its numbers are not shrinking, its soldiers are not always unhappy, and it is not short of supplies.
770: Even if an army has many loyal soldiers, it cannot last without good leaders.
771: A soldier warns the enemy: do not stand against my king. Many who once stood before him are now only stones that mark where they died.
772: It is better to hold a spear that missed an elephant than an arrow that killed a rabbit in the forest.
773: Having no fear in battle is called great bravery. But helping your enemy when he is in trouble is the sharpest edge of that bravery.
774: A hero throws his only spear at an elephant and looks for another weapon. He finds one stuck in his own body, pulls it out, and smiles.
775: For truly brave soldiers, even blinking when the enemy’s spear comes at their angry eyes counts as running away.
776: A hero counts his days and calls every day wasted on which he did not get a wound in an honorable fight.
777: For people who want fame that spreads across the world and do not worry about their own lives, wearing the warrior’s ankle ring is a true decoration.
778: Soldiers who do not fear for their lives when war comes do not lose their eagerness to fight, even if the king angrily stops them.
779: Who could blame for failure those who die keeping the promise they made?
780: If a soldier can die in a way that brings tears to the eyes of the king who cared for him, that death is worth begging for.
781: What is as hard to gain as friendship? And once you have it, what protection is as hard for any enemy to break?
782: Friendship with good people grows like the moon getting bigger each night. Friendship with fools shrinks like the moon after it is full.
783: Friendship with good people is like a great book. The more often you go back to it, the more you enjoy it.
784: We make friends not just to laugh together, but so that when a friend goes the wrong way, we can step in first and correct them.
785: Friendship does not need you to meet often or know each other for long. Thinking and feeling alike is enough to make true friends.
786: Friendship that only makes the face smile is not real friendship. Real friendship makes the heart smile inside.
787: A friend stops you from doing what would ruin you, guides you onto the right path, and shares your pain when trouble comes anyway.
788: When a person’s clothes slip, the hand rushes to catch them. In the same way, a true friend rushes right away to end a friend’s trouble.
789: Where does friendship sit like a king on a throne? In always being ready to hold up a friend in every way you can.
790: When friends go around saying, “He means this much to me, and I mean that much to him,” the friendship becomes cheap, however nicely they praise it.
791: Nothing is more harmful than making friends without first checking a person carefully. For loyal people, once a friendship is made, they cannot walk away from it.
792: If you make a friend without checking that person again and again, the friendship will bring you pain so bitter it could kill you in the end.
793: Make someone your friend only after you know their character, their family, their faults, and the people they spend time with.
794: Make friends with someone from a good family who feels ashamed of doing wrong, even if it costs you something.
795: Find and keep friends who can make you cry with hard truths, scold you sharply when you are wrong, and understand how the world works.
796: Even bad times have one good side. They are a ruler that measures how far your friends and relatives will really go for you.
797: The real gain for a person is to give up friendship with fools completely.
798: Do not think about things that make your spirit weak, and do not make friends with people who will leave you when trouble comes.
799: Friends who left you when you were falling will burn your heart, even if you only remember them at the hour of your death.
800: Hold on to the friendship of good, blameless people. Leave the friendship of the wrong people, even if you have to give something up to do it.
801: What is a long-standing friendship? It is one that never minds, in any way, the freedoms an old friend takes because you are close.
802: The freedoms friends take with each other are part of friendship. Good people should welcome those freedoms and enjoy them.
803: What good is a friendship of many years if you will not accept what your close friend does, as if you had done it yourself?
804: When close friends do something for you without asking, wise people are happy about it, because it came from someone they love.
805: If a friend does something that hurts you, think that it came either from not knowing better or from being so close that they felt free to do it.
806: People who know what true friendship is will not leave old friends, even when that friendship causes them loss.
807: People whose friendship has grown through many years of love do not stop loving, even when their friends do things that ruin them.
808: Some people trust a close friend so much that they will not listen when others talk about that friend’s faults. For them, the day the friend really does wrong is a good day, because it proves their trust.
809: The world loves people who never leave friends whose friendship has lasted, unbroken, for many years.
810: People who never lose their good feelings for old friends, even when those friends make mistakes, are loved even by their enemies.
811: Even when bad people act so fond of you that they seem to drink you in, it is better for that friendship to shrink than to grow.
812: Unworthy people become friends when they can get something and leave when they cannot. It makes no difference whether you gain or lose such friends.
813: A friend who measures what he can get, a person who loves only for money, and a thief are all the same.
814: It is better to be alone than to have friends who are like an untrained horse that throws its rider off in the middle of a battle.
815: It is better never to have the poor friendship of small-minded people than to have it. They will not protect you, even when you have done everything for them.
816: Being a stranger, or even an enemy, to wise people is worth ten million times more than being a very close friend of a fool.
817: What you get from your enemies is worth a hundred million times more than the friendship of people who only laugh along with you.
818: Some people pretend they cannot help and so spoil a job that could easily be done. Let your friendship with them quietly fade without saying anything.
819: Friendship with people whose actions and words do not match hurts you even in a dream.
820: Do not get even a little close to people who are friendly with you in private but say bad things about you in public.
821: The friendship of people who spend time with you but are not with you in heart is like an anvil, the iron block a blacksmith hammers on. When the time is right, they will strike you down on it.
822: The friendship of people who act like your own family but are not will keep changing, like the heart of someone whose love depends on being paid.
823: Even if they have studied many good books, people who are not good inside find it hard to become truly kind-hearted.
824: Watch out for tricksters who smile sweetly with their faces while their hearts are bitter toward you.
825: Never trust, in anything at all, the words of people whose hearts are not one with yours.
826: Even when enemies say good things as if they were friends, people soon see what their words really mean.
827: Do not trust an enemy’s polite, bowing words. A bow bends low only so it can shoot and do harm.
828: A weapon may be hidden in the hands an enemy folds before you in respect, and the tears they cry are just the same.
829: When people make a big show of friendship but secretly look down on you, smile back at them on the outside, but let that friendship die inside you.
830: When the time comes that you must treat an enemy like a friend, be friendly on your face but keep them out of your heart, and drop them when you can.
831: What is foolishness? It is grabbing what hurts you and letting go of what would help you.
832: The worst foolishness of all is wanting to do things you should not do.
833: Feeling no shame, not looking for what is worth having, having no love, and caring about nothing: these are the habits of a fool.
834: No one is a bigger fool than someone who has studied, understood, and even taught others, yet does not live by what they learned.
835: In just one life, a fool can do enough wrong to fall into a hell of suffering that lasts through seven future lives.
836: When a fool takes on a job he does not know how to do, the job fails, and he also ends up in chains.
837: When a fool becomes very rich, strangers enjoy his money while his own family goes hungry.
838: When a fool gets hold of something valuable, he is like a person who is already crazy and has also become drunk.
839: Friendship with fools is very sweet, because when it ends, saying goodbye causes no pain at all.
840: A fool walking into a meeting of wise people is like putting dirty feet on a clean bed.
841: Of all the things a person can lack, lacking good sense is the real poverty. The world does not count lacking other things, like money, as real poverty.
842: When a fool happily gives something away, it is only because of the good luck the receiver earned from past good deeds.
843: Fools bring more suffering on themselves than even their enemies could cause them.
844: What is stupidity? It is the proud belief that says, “We are the wise ones.”
845: Pretending to know things you never learned makes people doubt even the things you really do know well.
846: If you do not get rid of your faults, then carefully covering your body with clothes is just foolishness.
847: A fool who does not keep good advice, or lets an important secret slip, does great harm to himself.
848: A person who will not do what is right when told, and cannot figure it out alone, is like a sickness that lasts until the day they die.
849: If you try to make a fool see the truth, you end up looking like the fool, because the fool is sure he already sees everything his own way.
850: A person who denies what the wise people of the world say is true will be seen as a demon and kept away from others.
851: Wise people call hatred a disease. In every living being, it grows the ugly habit of not getting along with others.
852: Even if someone who wants to fight with you does things that hurt you, the best thing is not to hurt them back out of hatred.
853: If you get rid of the painful disease called hatred, you will win fame that never fades.
854: When hatred, the worst of all pains, is gone, it gives the greatest of all joys.
855: Who could ever beat people who can turn away from hatred whenever it rises inside them?
856: For a person who thinks it is nice to get ahead by fighting with others, failure and ruin are very close.
857: People whose harmful minds are set on fighting can never see the true way that leads to success.
858: Staying away from hatred brings good things. Whoever keeps adding to it brings ruin running toward them.
859: When good times are coming, a person does not even think about hatred. When they are bringing ruin on themselves, they try to make it bigger.
860: All painful things come from hatred. From friendliness comes the proud treasure called true goodness.
861: Do not pick fights with people stronger than you. But do not be slow to stand against people who are weaker.
862: A person who has no love for their own people, no strong friends to help, and no strength of their own, how could they ever beat a strong enemy?
863: A person who is scared, does not know things, cannot get along with others, and will not share is very easy for enemies to beat.
864: A person whose anger never goes away and who cannot control himself is easy for anyone to beat, at any time and in any place.
865: A person who does not follow the right way, does not do what is proper, does not care about shame, and has no good character makes his enemies happy.
866: It is good to have as an enemy a person who is blinded by anger and full of endless greed, because he will beat himself.
867: If someone stays close to you but does bad things, you should certainly make them your enemy, even if it costs you something.
868: A person with no good qualities and many faults ends up with no friends to help, and that makes it easy for enemies to win.
869: People who fight will never be far from joy if their enemies are both foolish and scared.
870: A person who will not take even the small, easy win of fighting an enemy who knows nothing will never become famous.
871: Hatred has nothing good in it. No one should want it, not even as a game or a joke.
872: Even if you must make enemies of soldiers who use the bow as their plow, never make enemies of wise people who use words as their plow.
873: A person who is alone and still makes enemies of many people is more foolish than someone who has lost their mind.
874: The world is safe because of the greatness of a kind person who makes enemies into friends and lives that way.
875: If you have no one to help you and you face two enemies alone, make one of them your friend.
876: In a time of trouble, whether you have tested a person before or not, do not get too close to them and do not cut them off. Keep a careful distance.
877: Do not tell your troubles to people who do not already know about them, and do not show your weak points to your enemies.
878: Know the right way to act, build up your strength, and protect yourself well. Then your enemies’ pride will fade away by itself.
879: Cut down a thorny tree while it is still young. Once it grows hard, it will hurt the hand of the person who tries to cut it.
880: People who do not break the pride of enemies who hate them cannot really be called alive, not even as much as breathing.
881: Shade and water are pleasant, but they are bad when they make you sick. In the same way, your own relatives become painful when they do you harm.
882: Do not fear enemies who come at you openly like a drawn sword. Fear enemies who pretend to be your relatives or friends.
883: Fear the enemy within your own circle and protect yourself. When you are weak, it will cut you down as surely as a potter’s tool cuts clay.
884: If hidden hatred grows in a mind that will not change, it brings many troubles and turns a person’s own people against them.
885: If hidden hatred grows among relatives, it brings many deadly troubles.
886: Once fighting starts among people who were united, it is always hard to escape being destroyed.
887: A family full of hidden hatred may look joined together like a box and its lid, but it is never truly united.
888: A family with hatred inside wears itself down and loses its strength, like metal worn away by a file.
889: Even if hatred inside a group is as small as half a sesame seed, ruin is hiding inside it.
890: Living with people who do not truly agree with you is like sharing a small hut with a snake.
891: Of all the ways a careful person can protect themselves, the first and best is never to look down on the power of people who can do whatever they set out to do.
892: If a person acts without proper respect for great people, that lack of respect will bring him trouble from them that never goes away.
893: If a person wants to ruin himself, let him ignore all advice and do wrong to people who can destroy him whenever they want.
894: When weak people harm strong people, it is like waving to Death with their own hand to come and take them.
895: People who make a fierce and powerful king angry will not survive, wherever they run to.
896: A person caught in a fire may still survive, but people who keep doing wrong to the great will not escape.
897: If truly great people with fine character become angry with someone, what good are that person’s grand life and great riches?
898: If people as great as mountains are looked down on, or decide to ruin someone, even people who seemed firmly settled will be wiped from the earth along with their families.
899: When people with high ideals rise up in anger, even a king will be broken in the middle of his rule and lose his kingdom.
900: Even people with endless support and powerful friends cannot escape if truly great people become angry with them.
